rationale: Move from the runtime layer to core decision visibility and authority transition. Source reading shows sync_log assigns the new leader's decided_idx unconditionally, and the leader derives that index from the maximum decided among the promises that formed its prepare quorum; a follower that already decided a later entry but promises only after that quorum therefore receives an AcceptSync carrying a lower decided index. A five-node in-process probe is requested to observe whether a decided entry can revert to Undecided and be decided again.

investigations.question: Can a follower that already read an entry as Decided have its decided index lowered by a new leader's AcceptSync when it promises after that leader's prepare quorum, so the same entry is later reported Decided again?
investigations.hypothesis: Yes. A new leader's decided index is the maximum decided index among the promises that formed its prepare quorum. A follower outside that quorum can have decided further because it received an earlier leader's Decide while quorum members did not. When that follower promises later, handle_promise_accept sends it an AcceptSync whose decided_idx is the leader's lower value, and handle_acceptsync passes it to sync_log, which assigns decided_idx unconditionally. The follower's decided index decreases, read(index) changes from Decided to Undecided for an entry already applied, and the entry becomes Decided again after the new leader re-decides it.
investigations.discriminator: A five-node run in which entry 5 is decided with four accepting nodes but the Decide reaches only one follower, those nodes elect a new leader whose prepare quorum excludes that follower, and the follower's late promise triggers AcceptSync: the observed decided index and the Decided/Undecided status of the same index before, immediately after the sync, and after re-decision.

interpretations.rationale: Source establishes the mechanism but not yet the witness. handle_majority_promises sets the new leader's decided index to the maximum decided among the promises it has received (the prepare quorum); send_accsync then stamps every later promiser's AcceptSync with the leader's current decided index, and handle_acceptsync passes that value to sync_log, which sets the decided index without comparing it to the follower's existing value. A follower that promised during the prepare phase is part of that maximum; a follower whose Prepare is delayed until the leader is already in Accept is not, and set_promise for that later promise is called with check_max_prom false and does not update the maximum. If that follower had already learned a decision the quorum members had not, the AcceptSync lowers its decided index and read() reports a previously Decided entry as Undecided, contradicting the documented guarantee that a decided entry is not reverted and is safe to apply. The new leader then re-accepts and re-decides the entry after its accept quorum acknowledges, so the entry returns to Decided, exposing an at-least-once application hazard. The decisive uncertainty is whether the state can be built with real instances and legal message delays, which the registered five-node probe measures.
counterevidence: If the delayed follower's promise reaches the leader before the prepare quorum completes, its decided index participates in the maximum and no regression occurs.
If every member of the new leader's prepare quorum has also received the earlier Decide, the leader's decided index already covers the entry and the sync is not lowering anything.
The value of the entry is preserved by the sync, so this is a visibility and application-status defect rather than a divergence of decided values.
limitations: No execution receipt yet; the account rests on source reading and a constructed scenario that the probe must realize with real instances.
The run uses five nodes, unit batch size, memory storage and no snapshots; flexible quorums and snapshot-based sync are not exercised.
Whether an application observes the Undecided window depends on its sampling; the probe samples synchronously after the AcceptSync is processed.

scope.description: Five real OmniPaxos instances (pids 1..5) in one process, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1. Node 1 leads and decides entries 1..4 everywhere; entry 5 is accepted by 1,2,3,5 and decided by 1 after 1,2,3,5 accept, but the Decide reaches only node 5. Node 1 is then cut, node 2 is elected with promises from 3 and 4 only, and node 5's delayed Prepare makes it promise in Accept phase. Node 5's decided index and the status of the entry at index 4 are sampled before, immediately after the AcceptSync, and after the new leader re-decides.
assumptions: Messages are delivered synchronously to their addressed node when routed; omitted messages are dropped, which the library's own resend and prepare-request paths are designed to repair.
Holding one Accepted(5) reply from nodes 3 and 4 while node 5 promises models slow acknowledgement, not a Byzantine or corrupted message.
No ticks are called, so leadership is obtained only through try_become_leader and BLE elections do not occur.
excluded: Snapshots, flexible quorums, batching, reconfiguration and more than one delayed promise.

experiment.prefix: Build nodes 1..5 from ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2,3,4,5]} with MemoryStorage and settle. node1.try_become_leader(); settle so all five promise. Append Value(1..=4) with settle after each. Append Value(5): drain, deliver the AcceptDecide to every follower except node 4, settle, then deliver the Decide for index 5 only to node 5 so nodes 2 and 3 accept 5 but remain decided=4. Emit late_sync phase=before for node 5 (decided, status of read(4), leader1 decided, node2 decided/accepted). Purge all traffic to or from node 1, call node2.try_become_leader(), hold node 2's Prepare addressed to node 5, settle so nodes 3 and 4 promise and node 2 enters Accept and sends AcceptSync; deliver those AcceptSyncs and hold the Accepted(5) replies. Deliver the held Prepare to node 5, settle so its late Promise reaches node 2 and node 2 answers with AcceptSync carrying its decided index. Emit late_sync phase=after_sync (decided, decided_before, entry status, leader2 decided, regressed). Then deliver the held Accepted(5) replies, settle, and emit late_sync phase=after_redecide.

comparisons.description: After the AcceptSync, node 5's decided index is lower than before and the same index reads as undecided.
After the new leader re-decides, node 5 is back at decided 5, so the same entry was observed decided, undecided and decided again.
